function: Decentralized over-the-air aggregation of model differences with full-duplex MIMO AirComp; transceiver beamforming and computing frequencies come from closed-form alternating optimization, not a learned policy (p. 7-8).
system: Full-duplex D2D network of K devices, each with Nt transmit and Nr receive antennas (10 to 30 tested), residual self-interference, bandwidth 1 MHz, no RIS (p. 3, 9).
method: Non-learned alternating optimization (closed-form KKT beamformers, bisection) for the JC2 problem; the CNN is trained by decentralized federated SGD with local updates and AirComp consensus (p. 3, 7-8).
data_channel: Simulated channels: path loss 10^-3 x^-3.67 with Rayleigh small-scale fading, Rician residual SI channel; CNN trained on non-IID Fashion-MNIST across devices (p. 9).
test_conditions: Perfect global CSI; sweeps over antennas (10-30), residual SI (-75 to -50 dB), energy budget, devices, local iterations; 40 averaged experiments; no train/test channel mismatch (p. 4, 9-11).
baselines: Ideal error-free full-duplex scheme, half-duplex counterpart designed by the same method (Algorithm 2), and FD-Ign (minimum-MSE design of [27], [31] ignoring residual SI); all non-learned (p. 9-10).
metrics: Training loss and test accuracy versus training time, antennas, residual SI, energy budget, device count, and local iterations; training time (p. 10-11).
complexity: Order of complexity O(K max{Nt,Nr}^3) for FD design and O(K^2 max{Nt,Nr}^3) for HD design, from closed-form matrix operations (p. 8-9).
openness: none; Fashion-MNIST is public but only for the learning task, and no code or data link is given (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "small-scale Rayleigh fading" with its own path loss 10^-3 x^-3.67 and a Rician residual-SI model; a custom simulator, with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 10: "learning performance versus training time under different numbers of antennas" is a parameter sweep with the design and the CNN run anew for each setting; the paper never trains in one condition and tests in another.
q3_support: p. 10: "FD-Ign: The devices work in the FD mode and the system design is obtained from Algorithm 1" but ignoring the SI term, so FD-Ign is a variant of the proposed design; Ideal and HD are the paper's own non-learned schemes, and no earlier published aggregation design is simulated.
q4_support: p. 8: "The corresponding computational complexity is" O(K max{Nt, Nr}^3) for the FD design (Algorithm 1); p. 9: "The corresponding computational complexity is" O(K^2 max{Nt, Nr}^3) for the HD design (Algorithm 2).
q5_support: p. 9: "on the Fashion-MNIST dataset [45]" is a public dataset of the learning task alone, the channels are simulated, and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Included as area 7: over-the-air federated learning with AirComp consensus in full-duplex MIMO. The physical-layer design is classical optimization (Algorithm 1, p. 8), so it passes the learning check only through the rule for federated learning over the air (learned element is the CNN trained across devices); the reviewer should confirm. q3 is borderline: FD-Ign is called consistent with the minimum-MSE designs of [27], [31] (p. 10) but is built from Algorithm 1 without the SI term, so it is treated as an ablation.
